# ISSUE-56 implementation plan

Make unsuccessful implementation attempts visible immediately, preserve operator guidance for review, and prevent rejected or unmerged findings from becoming current agent guidance.

**Shape: Involved.** The acceptance criteria form one recovery workflow across execution, sandbox input, bundle compilation, CLI output, and submission; changing only the PASS verdict would leave the feedback loop intact. Keep these coupled changes together for one plan review and validation cycle.

## What we know

- `ExecuteWork` skips planning whenever design/test artifacts exist (`internal/workflow/engine.go:518`), regardless of a rejected review. It already forwards `WorkOptions.Instructions` to planner, developer, tester, and reviewer prompts (lines 553, 694, 742, 889).
- After checkpoint publication/recording, implementation is unconditionally PASS (`internal/workflow/engine.go:706–730`); tester execution and trusted validation immediately follow. `SummarizeImplementationChanges` uses Git status/diff and active lessons, but does not read IMPLEMENTATION.md (line 1058).
- `Checkpoint` cleans ephemeral markers and only commits staged changes (`internal/workspace/worktree.go:362`). Active-only report writes must not count as implementation. PR execution uses `PRRevision.LocalHeadSHA` (`internal/workflow/engine.go:512`).
- `compileHarnessBundle` embeds rendered WORKUNIT.md into SYSTEM_PROMPT.md (`internal/workspace/worktree.go:705`); `renderWorkUnitMarkdown` includes all artifact bodies under Prior Artifacts (line 890). This reintroduces implementation lessons into subsequent prompts.
- Lessons are already copied into implementation artifacts, and harvesting already filters for merged linked PRs (`internal/workflow/lessons.go:21`, `HarvestLessons`). Preserve that merge boundary.
- Native Codex and delegated harnesses accept interactive follow-ups in coordinator-owned loops (`internal/sandbox/native.go:287`, `delegated.go:170`, `opencode.go:130`, `omp.go:216`). `RunResult` currently has no guidance collection (`internal/agent/runner.go:25`); `WorkerOptions` is the transport to those loops (`internal/sandbox/worker.go:30`).
- Submission loads the issue before checkpointing and calls FindDraftPR/CreateDraftPR later (`internal/cli/submit.go:61`, 113, 156). Status prints verdict/producer but not the artifact summary (`internal/cli/status.go:111`). Issue PR descriptions attach artifacts (`formatDraftPRBody`); PR revision submission currently projects only rebase context (`internal/pr/service.go:764`, `internal/pr/rebase_projection.go:42`).
- Artifact metadata accepts arbitrary string fields and FAIL is already a valid verdict (`internal/contract/artifact.schema.json`). `lease.Manager.updateArtifact` computes content hashes and selects attestation fields explicitly (`internal/lease/manager.go:1328`); steering text need not enter attestations or require a schema change.
- The current planning snapshot has no usable Git metadata (`git status --short` reports “not a git repository”). Repository-backed verification must create temporary repositories.

## What we're assuming

- “Blocked” means an explicit developer outcome, such as a leading status/verdict or heading saying “Blocked before implementation”, followed by its reason, rather than any incidental mention of the word. Confirm representative reports in fixtures first; implement a bounded, documented parser with negative cases for quoted/resolved blockers.
- Guidance count means delivered nonblank operator messages, with the flag counted once per role and each accepted follow-up counted once. Define the hash as SHA-256 of the UTF-8 JSON array of those messages, in delivery order, so boundaries are unambiguous. Tests will pin this representation.

## Open questions

- “Before any GitHub call” conflicts with submit's current need to read authoritative state/issue over GitHub. Implement the strongest local early rejection possible using the persisted claim/workspace and recorded base, before tracker resolution, then repeat against authoritative state after checkpointing. Inspect persisted claim/checkpoint formats in step 1 to establish what base is available locally. If a trustworthy local base is unavailable, explicitly record that gap for reviewer decision; do not claim zero calls when only PR calls are prevented. Never allow local evidence to authorize publication.
- Reviewer visibility versus “never compiled into an agent SYSTEM_PROMPT.md”: use report files/explicit review attachments for lessons, including for reviewer agents, while keeping every role's system prompt lesson-free. Step 4 tests both prompt contents and review evidence availability.
- No live GitHub, paid harness, or OCI image is required for acceptance. Fake trackers and fake executables cover behavior; any unavailable platform integration is reported separately, without blocking implementation on external infrastructure.

## Architectural choice

Use checkpoint identity for the specified no-op decision, not working-tree counts, report prose, or an empty-tree heuristic. Compare issue checkpoints to the approved base and PR checkpoints to the revision head captured before this execution mutates it. A blocked report independently fails even if files changed. Preserve existing fenced checkpoint/publication order and write the resulting FAIL through UpdateArtifact before returning. Do not invent commits to make empty work publishable.

Keep execution guidance separate from RoleAttestation: coordinator-collected messages produce artifact metadata and report appendices. Keep canonical plans separate from steering appendices so review binding and unchanged-plan detection compare actual PLAN.md/TEST_PLAN.md content, not injected guidance.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. **Establish regression fixtures and local submit evidence.** Extend `internal/workflow/engine_test.go`, `recovery_test.go`, `internal/cli/execution_test.go`, `issue_recovery_test.go`, and `internal/pr/service_test.go` using existing local mock/fake-runner patterns and temporary Git repositories. Inspect `internal/cli/claim_helpers.go`, `internal/workspace/checkpoint_state.go`, and persisted claim APIs for an early read-only empty-submit check. Add a small workspace ancestry/count helper in `internal/workspace/checkpoint_state.go` (with its tests), using hardened Git execution and errors on missing/unresolvable commits.
2. **Track delivered guidance.** Extend `RunRequest`/`RunResult` in `internal/agent/runner.go`, adapter paths in `adapters.go` and `isolated.go`, and `WorkerOptions` in `internal/sandbox/worker.go` with coordinator-owned collection plumbing. Add a delivery callback to the accepted follow-up paths in `native.go`, `delegated.go`, `opencode.go`, and `omp.go`; collect only messages actually forwarded, not empty input, rejected input, or agent output. Use one shared collector/encoding helper (new `internal/agent/guidance.go`) and tests; avoid duplicate recording through nested loops. Do not enable new harness capabilities or change isolation. Flag guidance reaches headless/OCI runs through the same request path; interactive capture applies to existing supported follow-up loops.
3. **Record implementation outcomes and steering.** In `ExecuteWork` capture the PR starting head before checkpoint updates; safely read the developer report, parse explicit blocked outcomes, retain the report alongside the existing change summary/lessons, and append a clearly delimited guidance appendix. Add bounded helpers in new `internal/workflow/implementation.go` and `guidance.go`. Write report files with safefs. Set FAIL and a summary containing the blocked reason/no-op explanation when applicable, preserve UpdateArtifact errors with wrapping, update returned state, and return an issue-specific rerun command (`swarm issue work N --phase implement`, or `swarm pr work P --phase implement`). Return before tester creation and required checks. Normal changes remain PASS. Add artifact metadata `operator_steered=true`, `guidance_count`, `guidance_sha256` only when guidance exists. Apply the same report/metadata path to planner, reviewer, and tester artifacts, preserving first-line review verdicts and appending after canonical role content. Capture reviewer-only output through its existing read-only output import, not a sandbox write bypass.
4. **Separate current context from previous attempts and lessons.** Refactor `compileHarnessBundle`/`renderWorkUnitMarkdown` in `internal/workspace/worktree.go`, and `CompilePRHarnessBundleAt` in `pr.go`, to render role-aware context. Map planner to design/test-plan, developer to implementation, tester to validation, reviewer to review. Present existing same-role artifacts under “Superseded previous attempt”, with their verdict and an explicit statement that they are not current findings; preserve applicable other-role context. Remove What we learned sections from all prompt-bound artifact bodies, including alternate heading levels and trailing sections, without discarding following non-lesson sections. Never read active LESSONS.md into SYSTEM_PROMPT.md. Preserve complete original reports for reviewers/PRs in separate evidence attachments; prevent prompt reintroduction through WORKUNIT.md embedding. Keep trusted base `.swarm/rules/lessons.md` loading unchanged. Add workspace compiler tests for every role and PR wrapper.
5. **Repair rejected-plan routing.** In `Preflight`/`rolesForPhase` and `ExecuteWork` in `internal/workflow/engine.go`, select planning for default all when the latest applicable review is CHANGES_REQUESTED; stale rejected reviews must not override a newer approved review. Snapshot rejected canonical plan/test digests and findings before updates. Tell the planner to address those findings, including the interactive awaiting-plan bundle. Compare the two new canonical content digests to the rejected pair before recording/reviewing; reject an identical pair with actionable feedback and no reviewer invocation. Changing either document permits normal review, with fresh bindings. Do not auto-approve, change gate semantics, or loop indefinitely. Extend engine recovery and PR service tests.
6. **CLI and publication visibility.** Register `--instructions` on `newWorkCmd` in `internal/cli/work.go`, bound to existing `WorkOptions.Instructions`, matching PR work. Update `newStatusCmd` to display failure summaries and steering count/hash; JSON already carries artifacts. In `newSubmitCmd`, reject zero commits in `base..head` before tracker activity wherever local evidence permits (step 1), and authoritatively recheck the exact checkpoint before validation, push, or PR lookup. Name the approved base SHA and rerun command; leave clean-head and claim fencing intact. Extend `formatDraftPRBody` with steering notices and full review evidence outside provenance JSON. Add `internal/pr/review_projection.go` and tests for an idempotent managed review-evidence section, invoked by `Service.Submit` on successful/retry publication paths, preserving human PR text and existing expected-head checks. Include steering metadata, role reports, and lessons for revised PRs as well as initial issue submissions; do not condition this on LastRebase being present.
7. **Prompt and recovery documentation.** Update only `internal/harness/templates/swarm/prompts/developer.md` to explain the Git-free snapshot, temporary repositories for Git tests, and empty .git recovery. Add a scaffold assertion in `internal/harness/scaffold_test.go`. Update `docs/developer.md` under “Recovering from an Interrupted Run” with failure/status, steered rerun, rejected-plan recovery, and empty-submit behavior. Update `CHANGELOG.md`. Verify all command examples against Cobra registrations. Leave protected `.swarm/prompts/developer.md` unchanged; recommend the explicitly requested maintainer follow-up to sync it.
8. Run the tests in TEST_PLAN.md, then approved build/test/vet commands and `make check`. Preserve existing fence, trusted-base, approval-binding, and sandbox tests. Record any environment limitations honestly.

## Scope and review boundary

No coordinator protocol, credential handling, forced publication, new backend, or persistent attempt-history redesign. The existing current artifact store suffices to label an earlier attempt before its replacement. Review the local pre-network submission guard and canonical-plan/guidance separation carefully; these are the main design risks. No production or protected files are changed during planning.
